title: Study strategies for ADHD
examples: What is body doubling and how can I use it?
Can using a timer really help me focus better?
What kind of movement breaks are best for studying?

explain.say: Today we will learn some helpful study strategies for focus.
Body doubling means studying near another person working quietly.

draw.text: Body Doubling: Study with a friend

explain.say: A simple example is studying math problems with a family member nearby.
Next we will look at using timers to manage our study time.
Try setting a timer for twenty minutes to read a chapter quietly.
Movement breaks help your body release extra energy while you learn.

faq.q: Does body doubling mean I have to talk to the other person?
faq.a: No, it does not mean you have to talk. You just need to be in the same quiet space working on your own tasks.
asks: Do I need to talk to them?

faq.q: If I use a timer, should I work until the buzzer rings?
faq.a: Yes, try to focus completely until the timer goes off. This trains your brain to concentrate for set amounts of time.
asks: Should I stop when the timer rings?
How do I use the time limit?

faq.q: How long should my movement breaks be?
faq.a: Short breaks are best, maybe two to five minutes. This is enough time to move around and reset your focus.
asks: What is a good break time?

faq.q: Can I do all these things at the same time?
faq.a: It is better to try one strategy at a time first. Once you are comfortable, you can combine them.
asks: Which one should I start with?

faq.q: Are these strategies only for big subjects like science?
faq.a: No, these strategies work for all subjects, like history or English reading. They help with focus generally.

facts: Body doubling provides a sense of accountability to keep you on task.
Short, focused work intervals help prevent mental fatigue.
Movement breaks help release physical energy that can distract focus.
Consistency is key when practicing any new study skill.

quiz.say: Studying next to a calm friend without talking is called:
quiz.why: This technique uses another person's presence to help you stay focused.

wrong.0: Group study usually involves discussion, which is different from quiet presence.
wrong.1: Pair work suggests you are working together on a task, not just near each other.
wrong.2: While it is an accountability tool, the specific term for the action is body doubling.

quiz.say: Which activity is a good example of a movement break?
quiz.why: Stretching uses large muscle groups and gets the blood moving when sitting still is hard.

wrong.0: This is a distraction, not a planned physical reset for your body.
wrong.1: Writing is a fine motor skill task, not a full body movement break.
wrong.3: Reading is a cognitive task, not a physical movement break.
